title: IO Graph: Import and Export
description:
Allows to import and/or export IO Graph settings from/to a file.
It becomes very handy when working with multiple different IO Graph
configurations.

notes.body:
An example how the UI looks like:

![grafik](/uploads/27d6e3e4d33c5302379def3812f9c1c9/grafik.png)

Look nice

a small CI/CD error :
epan/uat.c:391: trailing whitespace.

Why not implement something like a "button drop-down" to switch between multiple I/O Graphs in the same profile? Using Export/Import doesn't look like a good flow to rapid switch between different graphs, and it doesn't really work with the profiles design.

I do not work a lot with profiles. I typically have only the default profile running. I think your proposal might be a good replacement for the _copy from other profile_ button?

If we go with the current proposal, the order of the buttons should be switched "Import" + "Export" to match the Coloring Rules dialog.

> I do not work a lot with profiles.

Pinging @BettyD in case she has any opinions to share as a profile power user.

I'm not sure I understand the goal of the change.

If the goal is the ability to append graph settings from another profile, I agree with @stigbjorlykke. A "Copy From" button like the one in color rules should be added.

If the goal is to clear current graph settings and import a new one from another profile, then I agree with @geraldcombs. The order of the buttons should be flipped to match color rules.

If the goal is to export the settings, an iographs file is already created for each new profile. An export button is a nice add, but you could just as easily copy the iographs file from one profile to the next via the operating system.

> but you could just as easily copy the iographs file from one profile to the next via the operating system.

I would advise against it because it's not a good user experience. Many users are not familiar with the way Wireshark stores its config files.

The general intention is to work with multiple different configurations for the IO Graph and switch between them. Having an _Import_ and an _Export_ button for different configs feels very natural and is a very intuitive way to achive this in my opinion.

So true on your point about not many users being familiar with the way Wireshark stores its config files.

The optimal additions would be all three buttons; Imort, Export, and Copy From as it is in the color rules dialog box.

2c5a2599 offers 
- an explicit Export button
- an import button that adds graphs to the list (without prior clearance)
- the Copy from profile button is kept

Maybe we should use the current naming scheme for this filename instead of creating a new name? Here it should be `"/io_graphs"`.

We don't add `.uat` to any of the config files we have. I'm not sure if we should start doing this for import/export of this specific UAT?

I would recommend using a file extension in this case because it makes life easier when working with open file dialogs. It allows you to set a filter for the actual file extension and this makes it easier for the user to pick the right file.

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10209/diffs?diff_id=656567870&start_sha=2c5a2599ee1e584b2a22975ebc8f7521b7708773#97e9e93210cf080f66354cea23b9b5ad4cbd4c7b_506_511)
The name of this method is not correct when used from `::importGraphs()`. Maybe make a generic method `::copyFromFile()` and call this from here and from `::copyFromProfile()`?
Good idea! ef60cf63
I would guess the correct title here is "Import Graphs…".

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10209/diffs?diff_id=656567870&start_sha=2c5a2599ee1e584b2a22975ebc8f7521b7708773#97e9e93210cf080f66354cea23b9b5ad4cbd4c7b_533_540)
You are right! ef60cf63

Even if you don't actively use Profiles you should try using Profiles (and the "Copy from" button) for your different IO graphs. Personaly I find profiles easier to use than doing an import selecting a specific file in the filesystem. Unless you have hundreds of different IO graphs of course.

Also remember that the coloring rules Import and Export functionality was made before we had Profiles (and the "Copy from" button), and also here I find it easier to use Profiles to select a different set of rules.

I gave it a try but it did not work well for me. Switching between different profiles did only work properly when closing the IO Graph before switching the profile. (bug?)

This has a major drawback from my point of view. It takes 3 times as long compared to importing a new config while having the IO Graph open.

1. Changing the profile -> 1 scan trough the entire file
2. Opening IO Graph again -> 1 scan trough the entire file
3. Setting the interval to the desired value -> another scan through the entire file

When a single scan through takes multiple minutes it costs you a lot of valuable time.
Actually I was thinking about the "Copy from" button, which should be faster.
Storing of I/O Graphs dialog settings are inconsistent, that I would say is a bug. Some are stored and some are not stored, this must be all or nothing.
Ok this might be quicker.
